title: m07: ACNS neonatal continuity definitions and thresholds

locations.current:
| Continuous | Less than 2 s of attenuation below 25 µV |
| Discontinuous | Interburst intervals of at least 2 s, attenuated below 25 to 50 µV |
| Excessively discontinuous | Interburst intervals too long or too low for postmenstrual age, and bursts still contain some normal features. No numeric cutoff |
| Burst suppression | Invariant, abnormally composed bursts, interburst voltage below 5 µV, and no variability or reactivity |

It becomes **excessively discontinuous** only when the interburst intervals are too long or too low for the age, and the terminology deliberately sets no numeric cutoff, because the cutoff is the age-specific limit from the maturation tables.
ACNS defines continuous as less than 2 s of attenuation below 25 µV and discontinuous as interburst intervals of at least 2 s attenuated below 25 to 50 µV (Tsuchida 2013).
Excessively discontinuous means intervals too long or too low for postmenstrual age, with bursts that still contain some normal features, and there is no numeric cutoff.
interburst voltage below 5 µV, and no variability or reactivity (Tsuchida 2013)

recommendation: Keep the "25 to 50 µV" figure: it is the ACNS wording ("We define the IBI as a period in which activity is attenuated <25 to 50 µV pp for 2 seconds or more"). Clarify that it defines the interburst interval and is peak to peak. Fix "No numeric cutoff" for excessive discontinuity, which is wrong: ACNS defines it by the age-specific limits in its Table 4 (maximum IBI 35 s under 30 weeks, 20 s at 30 to 33, 10 s at 34 to 36, 6 s at 37 to 40). Continuous (<2 s of attenuation <25 µV pp) and burst suppression (IBI <5 µV pp, invariant, unreactive, no normal graphoelements) are correct as written.
